title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Deployment Runbook - Packaging, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback, Customer Requirements
author: Priya Khatri
summary: Comprehensive, production-ready runbook that consolidates deployment guidance for Redwood Private (VPC & on-prem), including packaging artifacts, reference architectures, pre-deployment customer requirements, day-2 operational procedures, and safe upgrade/rollback playbooks.
content:
Overview
This runbook collates the recommended practices and prescriptive procedures for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for SREs, deployment engineers, and solutions engineers during onboarding, initial deployment, and operational life-cycle activities (day-2).

Goals
- Provide a repeatable, auditable deployment checklist for VPC and on-prem customers.
- Standardize packaging artifacts and installer expectations.
- Define day-2 operational procedures: health checks, scaling, backups, and incident triage.
- Provide a conservative, tested upgrade and rollback procedure with verification gates.
- Capture customer requirements and handoff artifacts required for onboarding.

Prerequisites and ownership
- Deployment owner: eng-private-deployments (primary) / customer success (support)
- Pre-reqs: network connectivity (customer VPC CIDR, peering/VPN details), KMS/HSM integration plan, artifact repository access, targeted hardware inventory (GPU type, RAM, local NVMe), and maintenance window.
- Slack channel: #private-deploys-<customer>-<env> (create on project kickoff).

Reference architectures (summary table)
| Use case | Network topology | Typical instance types | Storage pattern | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Small on-prem PoC | Single rack, NAT to control plane | 8x A10G or equivalent (4 GPU) | Local NVMe + NFS for common artifacts | Single-region, manual autoscale |
| Enterprise VPC (SLA) | Private subnets + transit gateway + peering | Multiple p4d/p5d pools + CPU controllers | EBS gp3 for state, S3 compatible object store | Use Dedicated reserved pools; enable private control plane |
| Air-gapped on-prem | Isolated network, offline KMS | Replicated GPU nodes, smaller batch sizes | Local artifacts mirrored via offline repo | Requires on-site engineer & packaging bundle |

Packaging and installer artifacts
1) Packaging artifacts delivered to customer:
   - release_manifest.json (SHA256 checksums, image tags, component versions)
   - helm charts / kustomize overlays for control-plane components
   - container images (OCI tarballs) for air-gapped installs OR registry credentials for VPC installs
   - operator bundle (if using operator deployment)
   - packaging checksums.sig (PGP signature)
2) Expected package layout for on-prem bundle (example):
   - /bundle/
     - images.tar.gz
     - charts.tgz
     - release_manifest.json
     - install.sh
     - README_install.md
3) Packaging verification steps (pre-delivery):
   - Verify release_manifest signatures.
   - Test bundle install in staging air-gapped lab (documented matrix: GPU type x kernel version).
   - Validate health probes and sample inference against local test models.

Pre-deployment customer checklist (must be completed before deployment)
- Network
  1. Confirm CIDR ranges and inbound/outbound rules for control plane and nodes.
  2. Provide details for VPN/Transit/Peering, IP allowlists, and proxy requirements.
- Security
  1. KMS/HSM access plan and key rotation policy.
  2. RBAC matrix and SSO provider metadata.
- Hardware & OS
  1. Node inventory: GPU model, driver version, NVMe capacity.
  2. OS image (Ubuntu 22.04 preferred) and kernel version.
- Storage
  1. Object store endpoint for model artifacts, snapshot policy.
  2. Persistent volume class mapping for checkpoints and logs.
- Maintenance
  1. Approved maintenance windows (primary + fallback).
  2. On-call escalation list and remote access plan.

Day 0: Deployment procedure (VPC / on-prem)
1) Kickoff and prechecks (owners: deployment engineer, solutions engineer)
   - Validate manifest (release_manifest.json) signatures and checksums.
   - Confirm network routes and DNS resolution to control plane.
2) Bootstrap control plane
   - Run install.sh (or operator apply) using provided overlays.
   - Wait for control plane pods to reach Ready state (kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready).
3) Provision worker pools
   - Apply GPU node pool manifests. Verify node labels and taints: `node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu=true`.
   - Ensure nvidia-driver daemonset reporting all GPUs.
4) Post-install validation (smoke tests)
   - Inference smoke test: run sample workload for 60s, verify latency < expected SLO (see below).
   - KV cache and prefix cache sanity tests.
   - Verify metrics ingestion to prometheus endpoint.
5) Final handoff
   - Deliver runbook, dashboard links, and backup schedule to customer.

SLOs, monitoring, and alert thresholds
- Production inference request latency (p50/p95): p50 < 30ms, p95 < 200ms for short prompts (<512 tokens) - adjust per customer SLAs.
- GPU utilization: critical alert if sustained > 90% for 10m without autoscale activity.
- Queue depth: warn if backlog > 2x baseline for more than 5m.
- Disk usage: warn at 75%, critical at 90%.
- Replica health: critical if > 10% replicas not Ready for 5m.
- Alerts should map to runbook playbooks in PagerDuty with clear escalation.

Day-2 operational playbook (daily/weekly tasks)
Daily
- Check cluster component health (control plane, scheduler, runtime) and quick metrics snapshot.
- Confirm nightly backups completed and snapshot integrity.
- Review high-latency traces and customer-reported issues.
Weekly
- Run load test against staging with representative workload.
- Validate quantization/precision profiles against sample evals.
- Rotate PVC credentials for object store (if required).
Monthly
- Review kernel/driver compatibility and schedule maintenance for driver upgrades.

Incident triage template
1) Ingest: collect request id, route, model version, node id, and full trace.
2) Triage: determine whether issue is control plane, runtime, or infra.
3) Mitigate: scale additional compute, divert traffic to fallback model, or enable cache warmup.
4) Remediate: apply fix (restart pod, cordon node, apply hotfix).
5) Postmortem: file incident with timeline, impact (tokens, customer-facing), RCA, and action items.

Upgrade procedure (safe path)
Pre-upgrade
1) Read release notes and verify compatibility matrix (driver/kernel/model runtime).
2) Create canary environment in customer staging that mirrors production.
3) Snapshot control plane DB and configuration; snapshot object store pointers.
Canary rollout
1) Apply upgrade to 5% of capacity (canary pools).
2) Run automated smoke and latency tests for 30-60 minutes.
3) Verify no regression in quality metrics (compare eval prompt sets).
Gradual rollout
1) If canary passes, increase to 25% then 50% with 10-30 minute observation windows.
2) Monitor error budgets, SLOs, and customer-reported issues; abort if thresholds breached.
Post-upgrade verification
1) Run full smoke and acceptance tests.
2) Confirm backups and monitoring alerts function.

Rollback procedure (when upgrade fails)
- Trigger conditions: sustained p95 latency regression > 2x baseline for 30m, error rate increase > 1% absolute for 15m, or critical control plane failure.
1) Immediately scale down upgraded pools and scale up previous version pools.
2) For stateful control plane components, restore from pre-upgrade snapshot (document snapshot id).
3) Validate data integrity (sample checksums, model artifacts).
4) Open incident and notify customer with rollback rationale and ETA for resolution.
Post-rollback
- Capture logs and create a forensic bundle (kubectl cluster-info dump, controller logs, kernel/drivers).
- Schedule root cause investigation and plan for a corrective patch.

Testing & verification matrix (minimal recommended tests)
- Smoke inference test (latency, correctness) - run after every change.
- End-to-end model quality eval - run on canary.
- Load soak test (4-6 hours) - run prior to major rollouts.
- Disk/IO stress and GC verification for model cache.

Customer requirements library (deliverables & templates)
- Standard deliverables: network diagram, contact & escalation list, maintenance windows doc, KMS integration template, registry access form.
- Templates included: network-reqs-template.yaml, kms-integration-checklist.md, hw-inventory-template.csv.

Ownership and contacts
- Eng private deploys (primary): eng-private-deployments@redwood.ai
- Oncall SRE: see PagerDuty schedule linked in customer onboarding doc.
- Solutions engineering: se-allocations@redwood.ai

Appendices
A. CLI snippets
- Verify pod health: `kubectl get pods -n redwood --selector=app=control-plane -o wide`
- Snapshot control plane DB: `redwoodctl backup create --target s3://<bucket>/snapshots --name pre-upgrade-20260310`
- Rollback worker pool: `kubectl set image deployment/worker-pool worker=image:previous`

B. Escalation matrix (short form)
- Level 1: Deployment engineer (15m)
- Level 2: SRE senior (30m)
- Level 3: Oncall engineering manager / Product (60m)

C. Change log
- 2026-03-01: Initial published version.
- 2026-03-10: Minor clarifications for packaging layout and added verification matrix.

If you are executing a customer deployment, use this runbook as the canonical source and copy it into the customer-specific confluence space; attach the exact release_manifest.json for traceability. For questions or exceptions, contact eng-private-deployments@redwood.ai.
